tools.name: find_windows
tools.description: List the free ad windows on the tower and the free city billboards, with monthly prices. Tower windows come first (floor 1 up, the cheapest floors first), then billboards (the most prominent first): use kind to get only one of them, and maxPrice to cap the monthly price. tools.name: get_window
tools.description: One window or billboard by id ("F47-S3" is floor 47, south face, column 3; "B-1234" is a city billboard): its monthly price and whether it can be leased now. When it can't, reason says why: taken (lit by a brand), reserved (paid, in review), paused, prize (a game prize, only its winner can lease it)

tools.name: get_prices
tools.description: Every floor's monthly price for a middle and a corner window, and the price range of city billboards, in US cents. The listed price is exactly what Stripe charges.

tools.name: start_lease
tools.description: Start leasing a free window or billboard for a brand. The ad (website, name, pitch, logo) is checked first; a refused ad costs nothing. tools.name: check_lease
tools.description: Where a lease stands: awaiting_payment, in_review (paid, a person checks it first), live, refused (nothing charged), rejected_refunded, refunded (the slot was taken while paying), expired (the link ran out unpaid) or ended, with a plain message.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_window, check_lease · Public sink: start_lease.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_window, check_lease · Public sink: start_lease

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
